Key vault

Your key belongs on your own computer

This preview can’t contact outside websites, so it can’t reach Harvard’s API. The live collection runs in the downloadable version of Chimera: open it in your browser, add your key there, and it’s encrypted with your passphrase before it’s saved.

No key yet? Request one from the Harvard Art Museums API page ↗.

At least 10 characters. It can’t be recovered, so keep it somewhere safe.

The vault is locked

This deletes the encrypted key from this browser. You’ll need to paste the key again to use the live collection.

The vault is open

How your key is protected

  1. Encrypted at rest. The key is sealed with AES-256-GCM in the browser’s storage. The encryption key is derived from your passphrase with 600,000 rounds of PBKDF2, and the passphrase itself is never saved.
  2. Decrypted only in memory. While unlocked, the key lives in the tab’s memory. Reloading or closing the tab locks it again.
  3. Can only go to Harvard. The page’s security policy blocks network requests to every site except Harvard’s, so nothing on the page can send the key anywhere else.
  4. Locks itself. After 30 minutes without use.
  5. Visible to you while in use. Harvard’s API takes the key in each request address, so it shows in your browser’s developer tools while you use the live collection.
